status: Runtime feasibility evidence; no enhancement enabled
scope: Original client Home scene, read-only REA-installed Frida probe. Not a battle GPU capture.
findings: Current NVIDIA compatibility table lists DLSS 5 3D-Guided Neural Rendering for RTX 50 only; RTX 30 is not officially supported. This is not proof that unofficial ports are fundamentally impossible.
DLAA is native-resolution temporal anti-aliasing; its output is not recovered higher-detail source geometry.

No ready NVIDIA runtime integration was found. Streamline integration requires resource tagging and frame constants, including motion-vector conventions, jitter and projection transforms. A screenshot-only postprocess does not supply that integration.
Home camera depthTextureMode=0 does not establish absence of custom depth or motion buffers in all battle modes.
Low lodBias is a candidate for an original-resource detail experiment, not proof of visible loss or proof that higher-detail meshes exist. No quality settings were changed.
limitations: Stripped QualitySettings getters prevented reading global AA, maximumLODLevel, mip limit and anisotropic filtering. Null values mean unknown, not disabled.
Camera allowMSAA is permission, not proof of effective antialiasing.
Loaded d3d12.dll does not establish the active graphics API.
No DLSS SDK/plugin installed, no rendered A/B enhancement result and no model-detail restoration demonstrated.
nextValidation: Inspect active original LODGroups and their renderer meshes before any reversible lodBias experiment; compare fixed-camera images and restore settings.

For DLAA integration, capture a private battle rendering frame and establish accessible depth, object/camera motion vectors, jitter and HUD-free color, then verify SDK support before implementing a hook.
Keep DLSS 5 separate from ordinary DLAA; current local hardware lacks official DLSS 5 support.
